title: Weather Concern Looms as Dani Busboom Kelly Eyes Nebraska Volleyball's Historic Wrigley Field Match - NewsBreak
text:
By Adityan Pillai ,
1 hours ago
Dec 14, 2025; Lincoln, NE, USA; Nebraska Cornhuskers head coach Dani Busboom Kelly reacts during the first set against the Texas A&M Aggies at Bob Devaney Sports Center. Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-Imagn Images
Dani Busboom Kelly is looking ahead to Nebraska volleyball’s upcoming match at Wrigley Field with a mix of excitement and caution. She spoke about how rare and special the opportunity is, calling it something that stands out in the sport.
At the same time, she did not ignore one factor that could influence how everything plays out.
Why Nebraska Volleyball Coach Dani Busboom Kelly Has Weather Concerns About Wrigley Field Match Nebraska volleyball will take on Missouri Tigers volleyball at Wrigley Field, turning a famous baseball stadium into a volleyball stage for the first time. The venue usually holds over 41,000 fans, which is far more than a typical indoor volleyball arena, allowing many more people to be part of this one-night event.
That is what makes this moment stand out. It is not just another match, but the first time volleyball will be played at Wrigley Field, a place known across sports. With a much larger crowd expected than usual, it gives the sport a bigger platform and a chance to reach more fans than a regular college match ever could.
Dani Busboom Kelly spoke about the upcoming Wrigley Field match during a recent conversation, sharing her thoughts on what it could mean for the program. In an interview with Randy Silver, she reflected on the scale of the opportunity and how rare it is for volleyball to step onto a stage like this.
She kept her focus on both sides of it. While the setting brings excitement and attention, there are still questions around how everything will play out.
READ MORE: Dani Busboom Kelly Issues Heartfelt Plea To Nebraska Volleyball Fans Ahead of Jordan Larson’s Home Finale
She also pointed out that playing outdoors in Chicago in September brings uncertainty, especially with how unpredictable the weather can be.
“I think it’ll be really unique and really fun and a really big deal to play in one of the most historic and well known sports in the world potentially. I’m a liitle skeptical about the weather so lets see how that turns out. Chicago in September so,” she said .
SEE ALSO: Nebraska Volleyball Stays Completely Silent Amid NCAA Transfer Portal Chaos
Chicago in September does not settle into one mood. One moment it feels like late summer; the next it carries a hint of fall, with winds picking up and clouds rolling in without much warning. For a sport like volleyball, that kind of shift matters, as even a slight breeze or a sudden change in air can alter how the ball travels and how players respond in real time.
